# Findings: unit 1.1 `[run]` and `[review]` tables

Reviewed: e91d1cecc356..a014a538d313, 13 files. Steps: all done.

## F1 — File-prefilled model and effort are treated as given, so changing the agent keeps the old harness's choices

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `cmd/ploopy/settings.go:157`, `cmd/ploopy/board.go:228-237`
- Situation: `.ploopy.toml` has `[run] agent = "opencode"`, `model = "custom/model"`, `effort = "max"`; nothing else sets them. The board opens and the author changes the agent to claude with `a`.
- Happens: `givenSettings` sets `g.harness, g.model, g.effort` from the values after the file fallbacks, so all three read as given. `normalize` therefore keeps `custom/model` and `max` when the agent changes: the board shows claude with opencode's model and effort. Enter either starts claude with the foreign model or fails with `--effort for claude must be one of medium, high, xhigh`.
- Should: A file value is a prefill, not something given as a flag or in the plan. Changing the agent should reset model and effort to the new harness's defaults, as it already does for last-run values and as the Triage column does for the same file values (`triageDraft.given` holds only flags). The handover states that `given.from(key, source)` still means locked and `fromFile`/`prefilled` is the file path; that is not what the value-based assignment on line 157 does.
- Test: none exists. `TestChangingTheAgentKeepsAGivenModelOrEffort` covers flags only; `settings_file_test.go` never changes the agent.

## F2 — A file effort without its agent is validated late or under the wrong name

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `cmd/ploopy/settings.go:250-255` (check runs before `fill`), `cmd/ploopy/settings.go:291-311` (`fill` resolves the harness), `internal/config/config.go:162-172` (skips when `agent` is empty), `cmd/ploopy/triage.go:116-123` (review message)
- Situation: `[run] effort = "max"` with no `[run] agent`, and the last run used claude; or `[review] triage_effort = "max"` with no `[review] triage_agent`, so the default claude is used.
- Happens: For the run, `config.Validate` cannot check the effort without an agent, and the check in `givenSettings` sees `s.Harness == ""` because `fill` has not run yet; the last-run claude is chosen later and the board carries `max` until Enter fails with `--effort for claude must be one of medium, high, xhigh`. For the triage, `validateTriage` fails with `the triage effort for claude must be one of medium, high, xhigh`. Neither names `[run] effort` or `[review] triage_effort`.
- Should: §3 says validation happens where the flag is validated today, with the same messages naming the key instead of the flag. After the harness is resolved (last run or default), the file effort should be checked there and reported as `[run] effort` / `[review] triage_effort`.
- Test: none exists for either case; `TestTheNewTablesAreValidated` always supplies an agent, so the config validator's skip is not exercised with the later resolution.

## F3 — The "from .ploopy.toml" source is not cleared when the board changes or replaces the prefilled value

- Class: slip
- Confidence: medium
- Where: `cmd/ploopy/board.go:257-267`, `cmd/ploopy/triage.go:56-66`, `internal/ui/board.go:493-496`
- Situation: `[review] triage_agent = "opencode"`, `triage_model = "deepseek/deepseek-flash"`, `triage_effort = "max"`; the board opens and the author changes the triage agent to claude.
- Happens: `normalizeTriage` replaces the model and effort with claude's defaults because `triageDraft.given` holds only flags, but the `sources` map is untouched. The board now renders `opus · from .ploopy.toml` and `high · from .ploopy.toml`, values the file never contained; the agent itself is also still labelled "from .ploopy.toml" after the author changed it. The Run column has the same stale label after any direct edit.
- Should: The board should say where the displayed value came from. Once the author changes a field, or normalization replaces it, the file source should be cleared (or remembered against the old value) so the badge cannot describe a value the file did not supply.
- Test: none exists; the new tests only inspect `field.Source` immediately after board construction.

# Findings: unit 2.1 `then` becomes the follow-up setting

Reviewed: 58153d509c08..bb08e4ad348a, 19 files. Steps: all done.

## F1 — A chained fix plan advertises "then review and fix", though a fix plan is never reviewed

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `cmd/ploopy/run.go:294` (HEAD `:379`), `cmd/ploopy/run.go:296` (HEAD `:381`), `cmd/ploopy/settings.go:476-477` (HEAD `:529-530`), `internal/control/control.go:118-124` (HEAD `:130-135`); the same value is printed through `cmd/ploopy/adjust.go:97,117,183` and `cmd/ploopy/report.go:66`.
- Situation: `ploopy review PASS --follow-up` (or follow-up turned on on the review board); the triage writes `PASS_FIXES.md`; the chain starts the fix plan. While a fix-plan unit runs, the author runs `ploopy adjust` or `ploopy status`.
- Happens: `overChosen` copies the review's follow-up into the fix plan's `chosenRun`, `runOnce` registers the fix plan with `FollowUp: &pick.followUp` and `review=false`, and `Describe` takes its ordinary-plan branch and appends `then review and fix`. Reproduced on the reviewed commit and on HEAD: the live status of a chained fix plan reads `no end action · then review and fix`. The fix plan does not go on to a review (D3; §5 item 3), and HEAD's own `followUpSuffix` already omits the follow-up text for `review.IsFix` plans, so the two descriptions disagree.
- Should: the fix plan's live status should carry no follow-up, or say "then stop"; pass `FollowUp` nil for a fix plan (or teach `Describe` the fix-plan case). A fix plan always ends the chain.
- Test: none exists. The fix-plan chain tests check which sessions start; none reads `control.List`/`Wanted.Describe` while a fix unit runs. A test that runs a review with follow-up and inspects the live status during its first fix session would show the string.

## F2 — Follow-up's explicit file false and its last-run prefill have no test

- Class: gap
- Confidence: high
- Where: `cmd/ploopy/settings.go:257-259` and `:341-345` (HEAD `:295-297`, `:382-386`); `cmd/ploopy/settings_file_test.go:174-216` (HEAD `:177-218`).
- Situation: `[automation] follow_up = false` is written explicitly (the reason the handover makes the field `*bool`), while `last-run.json` holds `followUp: true`; or nothing sets follow-up but the last run had it on.
- Happens: the new test covers file true and flag false only. Neither an explicit file false beating a last-run true, nor a last-run true being used when nothing else sets it, is exercised. Treating the explicit false as an absent key (e.g. checking `!= nil && *…`) or dropping the `prefilled("followUp")` guard in `fill` would still pass the whole suite; the first would let the last run override an explicit off, the second would forget the last run.
- Should: tests mirroring the existing "file beats last run" and "flag beats file" cases for follow-up, with an explicit false and with a last-run true, per §3's precedence and the handover's `*bool` rationale.
- Test: none exists.

## F3 — The Automation field keeps saying "from .ploopy.toml" after the author changes it

- Class: slip
- Confidence: high
- Where: `cmd/ploopy/board.go:374-379` (HEAD `:408-412`); the source comes from `given.prefills` (`cmd/ploopy/settings.go:63-68`), which the board's `OnChange` (`cmd/ploopy/board.go:218-221` at HEAD) never updates.
- Situation: `.ploopy.toml` has `[automation] follow_up = true`; the board opens showing `yes · from .ploopy.toml`; the author presses `n` to turn follow-up off.
- Happens: the re-rendered field shows `no · from .ploopy.toml`; the source string is computed once from `given.prefilled("followUp")` and is not cleared when the value changes. Reproduced with a test on HEAD. The same stale-source mechanism already affects the Run and Triage columns (1.1 F3); this unit added another field that inherits it.
- Should: clear the file source when the author changes the field (or when normalization replaces the prefilled value), so the board never claims the file supplied a value it did not.
- Test: none exists; the new file test only inspects the source before any edit.
